epic.title: Keys, secrets and domains: rotate everything (later), cull and harden
epic.description:
Every exposed or old key is rotated or confirmed dead through one parent Field guide with a phase per family (Mycelium's MYC-196 and MYC-6, the old VPS set, DropShipAuto, the old PhirstMaxxing app, a Stripe test key), names only, run later by Phil and not at the front of the queue; nothing was rotated in the run of 2026-11-28. The census files on the PC are checked and reported first, acted on only on Phil's word. The old VPS is checked before anything on it changes. Domains: three kept, the rest go through a keep-or-drop sitting under the standing rule that no domain lapses while any address on it is a login or recovery address; account-level hardening first, per-domain DNS work after the sitting.

## Order
keys.06 (census files, first in the unblock queue) then keys.07. keys.08 (the VPS) then keys.09 (port 3000) and keys.14 (a better home). keys.01 is the parent guide; its phases wait on MYC-209, keys.08 and phm.01 and run keys.02, keys.03, keys.04 and keys.05. Domains: keys.10, keys.11, then keys.13 (with mail.11); keys.12 any time; keys.15 after fin.14.

## Done means
Every key in keys.01 rotated or confirmed dead; the census exposure closed; port 3000 closed; every kept domain hardened and no domain lost while an address on it matters.

## Flags
- H2.2 [claude]: hardening every domain before the cull; account-level steps first (keys.12), per-domain DNS after the keep-or-drop sitting (keys.13). Not reopened.
- H9 flag 9: H2.5 and H2.7 were assumed; keys.08 and keys.09 are written check first.

## Dossier
The dossier is attached in Docs.

tickets.description:
## What
The parent Field guide for every rotation, names only, never values. Each phase points at its child: Mycelium's two exposed secrets (MYC-196), the rest of Mycelium (MYC-6, after MYC-209 lists the callers), the old VPS set (keys.02), DropShipAuto's tokens (keys.03), the old PhirstMaxxing app's keys (keys.04), the Stripe test key (keys.05). Each phase names the keys by role and where they live, runs the child, then checks the services that use them still work. **Nothing was rotated in the run of 2026-11-28**; Phil runs this later, not at the front of the queue.

## Why
H2 item 11: one "rotate everything" ticket as a Field guide, names only, alongside the Mycelium rotations already queued. H10: the Stripe test key added to it.

## Done looks like
Phases 2 to 7 each dated; every child closed; any key not rotated listed by name with the reason.

## Unlocks
A clean slate for E.sub and E.mail work that touches the same systems.

## Depends on
Nothing to start; phases wait on MYC-209 (Mycelium master secret callers), keys.08 (the VPS) and phm.01 (the old PhirstMaxx database).

tickets.title: Rotate: the old VPS set (the calendar agent's Anthropic key, four IONOS mailbox passwords, the API bearer token, the Google OAuth client secret)

Names only; new values go to Proton Pass and the place each lives.

## Why
H2 item 6: four were exposed in May and parked; a ticket, names only.

## Done looks like
Each of the four kinds rotated or revoked with the date; mail works on every client for each mailbox.

## Unlocks
keys.01 phase 4.

## Depends on
keys.01 (the parent order) and keys.08 (whether the VPS app is kept).

H2 item 10: Phil is not sure whether they were cleaned up; a ticket for Claude Code to check and report; revoke and delete only on his say. The largest known exposure; first in the unblock queue.

Nothing.

Nothing.

tickets.title: Port 3000 on the VPS: find what listens, close it
tickets.description:
## What
Claude Code finds what listens on port 3000 on the old VPS and whether anything needs it reachable from the internet (DropShipAuto runs on the same VPS: if port 3000 is DropShipAuto's, it is put behind the existing reverse proxy instead of closed). Phil approves, then the port is closed to the internet in the VPS firewall (IONOS Cloud Panel firewall policy, and the host firewall) and an outside scan confirms it.

## Why
H2 item 7 (assumed): port 3000 is open to the internet and nobody knows what listens; checked and closed.

## Done looks like
What listened is written down; port 3000 no longer answers from outside; DropShipAuto still works.

## Unlocks
Nothing further.

## Depends on
keys.08 (what the VPS is doing).

## Flag
H9 flag 9: this answer was assumed (H2.7). Check first, close on Phil's word.

## Red team
- Finding 4: If port 3000 belongs to a live tenant it goes behind the reverse proxy or the VPN rather than being closed; closed only on Phil's word.

steps_definition.title: Find and close port 3000 on the VPS

A table on the ticket with every domain and the six columns, and a keep-or-drop checklist ready for keys.11.

Phil goes down the keys.10 list and marks each domain keep or drop. A domain with any address still used as a login or recovery address cannot be marked drop; it is marked "keep until moved" and the mail migration's rows for it are linked. Nothing is cancelled in the sitting: for each drop, auto-renew is switched off at IONOS only after the last address on it is moved.

## Why
H2 item 1: a keep-or-drop sitting; the standing rule that no domain lapses while any address on it is a login or recovery address.

## Done looks like
Every domain marked keep, drop, or keep until moved; the list saved on the ticket.

## Unlocks

tickets.title: Domain hardening, account level first: registrar 2FA, transfer lock, auto-renew with a valid card, WHOIS privacy
tickets.description:
## What
At IONOS, the account-level steps that cover every domain at once: two-factor sign-in on the IONOS customer account (Menu, My account, Login and account security; authenticator app), with the 16-digit recovery code stored in Proton Pass; a check that every domain shows the transfer lock on (Domains, Renewal and Transfer); the payment card valid and auto-renew on for kept domains; WHOIS privacy on where IONOS offers it (note any cost). Nothing is bought.

## Why
H2 item 2: domain hardening, every domain, account-level steps first because they cover every domain in one go.

## Done looks like
2FA on and tested with one sign-in; the recovery code in Proton Pass; transfer lock on for every domain; the card valid; privacy status noted per domain.

## Unlocks
keys.13 (per-domain work).

## Depends on
Nothing.

## Flag
H2.2 [claude]: this hardens domains the cull is about to drop; the account-level steps go first because they cover every domain at once; per-domain DNS work waits for keys.11. Not reopened.

## Red team
- Finding 3: Auto-renew is removed from this account-level sitting: it is a per-domain, per-pound setting and belongs in keys.13 after the keep-or-drop sitting. Added here instead: the IONOS account's recovery email is the Gmail anchor (mail.08) before two-factor is enabled; registrar two-factor recovery codes go into Proton Pass.

tickets.title: Domain hardening, per domain after the sitting: DNSSEC, dangling records from old Wix, Squarespace, Shopify and Web Genie sites, TLS on live sites
tickets.description:
## What
For each domain kept in keys.11: Claude Code lists every DNS record and follows each CNAME to its end, flagging dangling records (final target does not exist, or a Shopify, Wix, Squarespace or Web Genie error page) left by old sites; Phil approves deleting each dangling record at IONOS. TLS is checked on every live site. DNSSEC at IONOS needs the paid Domain Guard or DNS Pro, so it is priced and switched on only for kept domains after Phil approves the cost, one domain first, checked with an outside validator. Null SPF and reject DMARC belong to mail.11.

## Why
H2 item 2: DNSSEC, dangling DNS records left by old Wix, Squarespace, Shopify and Web Genie sites, TLS on live sites; per-domain DNS work after the keep-or-drop sitting.

## Done looks like
No dangling record on any kept domain; every live site serves valid TLS; DNSSEC on for kept domains if Phil approved the cost, or "declined" recorded.

## Unlocks
Nothing further; mail.11 runs alongside.

## Depends on
keys.11 (which domains are kept) and keys.12 (the account hardened).

## Flag
H2.2 [claude]: per-domain DNS work after the keep-or-drop sitting. Not reopened.

## Cost
DNSSEC at IONOS needs Domain Guard (£1 the first year, then £15 a year, excluding VAT, checked 2026-11-28) or DNS Pro (£1 a month for six months, then £2.50 a month, excluding VAT). To be approved by Phil; nothing is bought in this run.

## Red team
- Finding 3: Auto-renew on for the kept domains only; sporebit.store and sporebit.org stay set to not renew.
- Finding 17: DNSSEC only where IONOS both registers and hosts the zone; otherwise the DS record is published only after the zone is confirmed signed. Mail is tested in the same sitting.
